commits.message:
build(workspace): enforce package boundaries and resolve workspace packages from source

Cross-package relative imports (../../<package>/src and dist) bypassed each
package's exports map and dependency declaration and were the direct cause of
the stale-dist phantom suite failures: vitest resolved @al-ft/midgard-core to a
gitignored dist while sibling files reached the same modules through src.

- ESLint no-restricted-imports bans ../<package>/src and ../<package>/dist for
  every workspace package (all file types), and bans the @/ alias inside
  midgard-sdk/src.
- Every package's exports map gains a `midgard-source` condition listed first,
  pointing at the TypeScript source. tsc (customConditions), typescript-eslint
  (via tsconfig) and vitest (resolve.conditions) resolve it, so typecheck, lint
  and test suites read sibling source and never need a prior build. Node at
  runtime ignores the condition and keeps resolving dist.
- midgard-core exports the two subpaths consumers had been reaching through
  src (retention-window-v1, codec/native-constants) and builds the former.
- midgard-sdk, midgard-fault-proofs and midgard-watcher gain root exports;
  da-committee-node gains subpath exports (and build entries) for the modules
  midgard-node's DA integration tests use.
- midgard-sdk/src drops the @/ tsconfig alias in favour of relative
  specifiers so consumers can compile it from source.
- Test-only workspace devDependencies replace the remaining relative reaches:
  midgard-validation -> midgard-fault-proofs, midgard-node -> da-committee-node,
  da-committee-node -> midgard-watcher.
- The 10k DA multi-process test bundles its helper through tsup's API with the
  same condition and all workspace packages inlined (plus a createRequire
  banner for CJS-only dependencies), so the child Node process never runs
  against a stale or missing dist either.
- midgard-sdk's @types/node range is aligned with the rest of the workspace
  (^22.17.0): consumers now compile midgard-core's zstd source under the
  sdk's own type set.

Verified with every dist directory deleted: workspace lint (error set
identical to HEAD: six pre-existing only-throw-error hits in midgard-manager),
typecheck for every package (da-committee-node's four pre-existing SDK-ABI
errors unchanged), and the sdk, validation, watcher, lucid-midgard,
da-committee-node suites plus the three midgard-node DA files. Every
remaining red was re-run at HEAD in the same worktree and reproduced
identically there. A full build still succeeds afterwards.
fix(ci): retire stale evidence gates and repair suites
A backup of non-contract-related changes made for the E2E test (branch can be deleted after the contracts are merged)
chore(lint): enable recommended type-aware ESLint rules

refactor(protocol): remove claim registry from canonical V1

Remove obsolete claim-registry plumbing and low-value identity pins, refresh measured deployment evidence, and reuse authenticated emulator deployment state across operator lifecycle scenarios. Stabilize the integrated runner around measured resource contention.
fix(node): unwrap retained DA payload before attestation decode

docs: fault-proof plan updates, catalogue re-audit, readiness and skills refresh

Fault-proof family plans and the fraud-proof catalogue status re-audit,
public testnet readiness updates, and agent skill/runbook refreshes.

feat(da-committee): StateQueueStatusV1 scanner, nullable ref-script outRefs, domain-tagged attestations

Scanner consumes the StateQueueStatusV1 sum (legitimate markers now scan as
attested — see #645); reference-script outRefs become nullable with
reconciliation; attestation signing is domain-tagged. The republish-optin
watcher polarity is skipped pending #646; suite 295 passed / 3 skipped.

feat(watcher,node): production watcher runtime, native chain sync, state-correction flows, watcher CI

Watcher: production L1-source runtime with fail-closed deployment-identity
verification on every evaluator call, native chain-sync integration (Go
binary is built locally and gitignored), state-correction flows, funding
seam, and the migrated test fixtures for the availability-challenge manifest
root (canonical response geometry, 28-byte deployment identities). Full
suite: 49 files, 768/768.

Node: workspace integration updates for the new watcher runtime plus the
dedicated watcher CI workflow, flake, and lockfile updates; l1-services
compose alignment. Deployment-manifest roster extended to the wave shape
(163 contract names / 156 reference-script roles / 157 auth token names)
with count pins re-derived; correction-lock construction takes the
availability-challenge policy; daPayloadTerminalOutcomes release authority
no longer null-trips on the manifest's new singular availabilityChallenge
root field (the plural fail-closed guard is retained). Operator fixtures
fund the exact required bond (900,000,000 lovelace, the env-derived
slashing penalty plus prover reward, which registered-operators now checks
with equality). Emulator suites blocked by the state_queue.mint envelope
regression run under a raised emulator maxTxSize documented against #649;
the scratch-cg1 publication-fit gate is skipped citing #649 and its
un-skip is the acceptance proof for the fix. The harmonic-uplc hub-oracle
case is skipped on an upstream plutus-machine bytestring-ordering defect
(#651) and the same policy stays covered by the real evaluator in the
initialization emulator suite.

feat(fault-proofs,validation): production workflow runtime and new family offchain

Fault-proofs: production workflow runtime with published reference-script
resolution (reference scripts required, inline attach removed), offchain
support for the min-ada, missing-native-script-utxo, native-script-invalid,
and network-id families, and emulator lifecycle coverage in both polarities.
The emulator harness applies the wave's re-parameterized correction-lock and
state-queue scripts (availability-challenge policy threaded through) and
publishes the now-oversized state_queue.mint through the documented
oversized reference-script escape — its 16,835-byte compiled size exceeds
the 16,384-byte L1 envelope, tracked as #649.

Claim-registry carriage completed across the offchain: computation-thread's
mint now mandates a claim-registry input in all three arms, so every
submitter and raw emulator driver that mints or burns the thread token
carries a prepared claim-registry mutation (family contracts self-prepare
the deployment-bound mutation; an optional prepared-mutation override and a
witness-roster reference-UTxO door are kept). Measured pins that the
mutation's reference input joins were re-derived, not modeled. A second
claim against a non-empty registry still needs the MPF proof deriver wired
into emulator journeys (#652); the Option B frontier pins shifted and await
a re-measurement campaign (#650).

Validation: network-id rejection wiring and machine updates matching the
onchain families; resolver proof-fit sweep artifact regenerated and
re-stamped against the wave's declared input closure.

The sweep's generation worker was migrated onto the current harness shape:
operator-lifecycle and witness reference-script rosters published before the
header clock is sampled, parties seeded at both base and enterprise
addresses, the authenticated validation-dispute control roster staged
through the shared helper, and the per-fixture prepare/semantic resolvers
plus canonical-decode item stage validators published as reference scripts
(dispute-scenario precedent throughout). The applied-identity pin for
resolver[1] (canonical_decode_item_semantic_v1.main.spend) moved with the
recompiled fraud-proof validator set and is re-pinned to the value the
regenerated sweep measures independently; the proof-item identity is
measured unchanged.

feat(core,sdk): ProvisionalWhole field view, availability-challenge surfaces, regenerated goldens

Core: FieldViewV1 ProvisionalWhole decoding chain with regenerated goldens;
deployment-manifest identity verification gains two semantics-preserving
caches (script-hash derivation LRU and a verified-finalized manifestId memo
keyed by the content-binding manifestId) — the identity re-hash still runs
uncached on every call, so any mutation either fails identity or misses the
memo. This removes the pathological repeated deep verification that made
fail-closed watcher evaluators re-derive ~163 script hashes per call.

SDK: availability-challenge v1 schemas (28-byte deployment_identity, 32-byte
da_bond_asset_name), canonical response geometry constraints
(tranche in [65536, 64MiB], chunk <= 15148, tranche-count coverage bound),
claim-registry and correction-lock tx builders, state-queue
MergeToConfirmedStateV1 support; the reference-script token roster gains
the availability-challenge spending/minting names. Known follow-ons:
initialization funds the correction lock at min-ada (#648); the emulator
claim-registry MPF proof deriver wiring (#652).
